summary: Terranovic is a website created for NASA Space Apps Challenge’s Field Shift challenge. It helps users explore how environmental conditions influence agriculture in Egypt. The website brings together NASA Earth observation data and information about climate, soil, and water to compare farming conditions across different areas. Users can explore maps, examine regional differences, and see how these factors may affect crop suitability and farming decisions. Terranovic makes complex environmental information easier to understand by connecting observations of Earth with the practical challenge of producing food. It encourages users to consider which crops may be better suited to particular regions and why. The website also emphasizes the value of reliable data when planning for sustainable agriculture. Through its maps and crop information, Terranovic demonstrates how satellite observations can support learning and informed discussions about farming. Its goal is to help people understand the relationship between Earth’s systems and agriculture in Egypt.
details:
Project Details

Terranovic is an interactive website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge’s Field Shift challenge. It helps users explore how climate, soil, and water conditions can affect crop choices and crop rotations, with a focus on Egypt. Users can explore map layers, compare regions, and view crop rotation reports that explain seasonal options and relevant growing conditions.

The website combines interactive mapping with crop information to make complex environmental data easier to explore. It considers factors such as temperature, water availability, soil conditions, crop season, and the limits of regional estimates. It also identifies evidence and data sources—including NASA POWER temperature information and GPM IMERG rainfall data for comparison—so users can understand the context behind the maps. The maps are intended for exploration and learning, not as precise farm-level prescriptions.

Terranovic aims to make Earth observation and agricultural information more accessible, encourage thoughtful crop planning, and support discussion about sustainable farming as environmental conditions change. Its creative element is the way it connects maps with practical crop rotation guidance, turning broad data into an interactive learning experience.

The project was built as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with interactive map and data-visualization features. It runs on standard computers and mobile devices and does not require specialized hardware.
